prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1484; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was westbound on the main roadway in Pasadena, Texas, approaching a signalized intersection when the vehicle was struck on the driver's side by Driver 2, who was proceeding southbound through the same intersection. The point of impact was the front quarter panel and driver door of Driver 1's vehicle, and the damage observed at the scene is consistent with a side impact of this type and force. Driver 1 reported neck strain and was transported for evaluation. The Passenger, seated in the front passenger seat, was also present in the vehicle, and both responding officers and the parties at the scene confirmed this. Scene photographs document several of the reported details, including the final rest positions and visible damage. No independent witnesses were identified at the scene or afterward. Responding officers found no indication of prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle, and Driver 1 is listed as an insured driver on the policy associated with the vehicle. Both drivers were cited for no violation pending further review of the signal timing.
